terms.grammar: suum, neuter of suus, with the dative cuique
evidence: Gell. 13.24.1: suum cuique per mē ūtī atque fruī licet
Cic. Leg. 1.19: ā suum cuique tribuendō (Lewis & Short s.v. ab)
terms.comment: Latin puts suum first; in the law books it is justice itself, suum cuique tribuere, to give each his due.

phrases.latin: sī quid est … quod ūtar, ūtor; sī nōn est, egeō. suum cuique per mē ūtī atque fruī licet
phrases.english: if there is something I can use, I use it; if not, I go without. As far as I’m concerned, everyone may use and enjoy his own
